bindings.label: Patient had a painless neck lump first noticed 6 years ago that recently grew rapidly

26-year-old male had a painless neck lump first noticed 6 years ago that had recently grown rapidly; he experienced agitation, irritability, excessive sweating, and discomfort while swallowing; he had previously been diagnosed with nodular goiter at other hospitals and intermittently took Euthyrox for several years; he reported childhood hearing impairment and language learning difficulties, with clinical examination indicating normal mental and physical development
Physical examination revealed a visible grade III goiter, with an enlarged, tough thyroid without palpable nodules and a clear boundary

Laboratory tests showed free thyroxine 9.99 pmol/l (normal 11.5–23.5), free triiodothyronine 6.07 pmol/l (normal 3.5–6.5), and thyroid stimulating hormone 2.401 μlU/ml (normal 0.3–5.0); thyrotrophin receptor, thyroglobulin, thyroperoxidase antibodies, carcinoembryonic antigen, thyroglobulin, and calcitonin levels were within normal ranges

Chest X-ray showed tracheal narrowing at the superior thoracic aperture; thyroid ultrasound revealed multiple hypoechoic signals in each lobe and isthmus of the thyroid and cervical lymph node enlargement; cervical computed tomography showed diffuse enlargement of each lobe and thickening of the thyroid isthmus, with numerous oval low- and slightly high-density nodules; electrical capacitance tomography results were consistent with signs of a nodular goiter
